finding_info.title: AI agent account defeating an anti-automation (CAPTCHA/bot) control
finding_info.desc:
An AI agent account called a CAPTCHA-solving service (2captcha, anti-captcha, CapSolver, CapMonster, DeathByCaptcha, NopeCHA, EZ-Captcha, SolveCaptcha, BestCaptchaSolver) or pulled in an anti-bot-detection "stealth" browser-automation toolkit (undetected-chromedriver, playwright-stealth, selenium-stealth, puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth, rebrowser, nodriver). This is the host-observable footprint of MITRE T1696 Anti-Automation Evasion (new in ATT&CK v20): an attacker who has prompt-injected or hijacked an agent drives it to defeat the automation checks (CAPTCHAs, bot detection) that separate humans from bots - to farm accounts, scrape behind a challenge, or beat rate limits at scale.
banken cannot see the CAPTCHA image or the solved token (those live in browser/LLM content), but it sees the agent *invoking the solver service or installing the stealth toolkit* on the host, which is the realised, host-side footprint. It deliberately does NOT key on the homegrown approach in T1696.001's own example (an ImageMagick script that transforms the challenge image), because ImageMagick is overwhelmingly benign - the service/toolkit footprint is the clean signal.
This is an "agentic AI detection" rule, scoped by account so the behaviour is clean signal from the agent even though it is noise on a human login (a human may legitimately use such a service). See rules/agent/README.md. (ATT&CK v20 files T1696 under the Stealth tactic, uid TA0005; banken keeps the attack.defense-evasion tag - same TA0005 uid the OCSF mapper knows - until a tree-wide v20 tactic-string remap, exactly as agent_impair_autonomous_defenses does for T1685.)
